records.summary: The property at 2214 Mission St is in the Mission Street NCT zoning district, where restaurants are conditional uses. The site sits inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which requires conditional use authorization for any restaurant in this sub-area and imposes operating conditions on all liquor establishments. The immediate block is extremely dense: 33 food and drink businesses within 500 feet, 14 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 feet, and 50 within 1,000 feet. Most significantly, this exact address has a withdrawn CUA from 2010–2012 for outdoor seating on an adjacent parking lot—the same concept now proposed—which was filed but withdrawn after nearly two years without a decision.

comparables.why_comparable: CUA for outdoor activity area at rear of existing bar/restaurant at 2323 Mission (187 m away), same NCT-MISSION district. Filed March 2017, approved December 2017 in ~9 months. This is a use decision approving outdoor seating.
comparables.key_takeaway: Rear outdoor areas for bar/restaurant uses on Mission Street in the NCT-MISSION district can be approved by CUA in under a year when the outdoor space is at the rear of the lot and serves an existing licensed establishment. Approval here suggests that location (rear vs. side parking lot) and existing-use status matter.

comparables.why_comparable: CUA for outdoor restaurant seating at rear of lot, 3481 18th St (132 m away), in RTO-M district. Filed August 2011, approved January 2012 in ~5 months. This is a use decision for outdoor seating.
comparables.key_takeaway: Rear outdoor seating for a restaurant one block away was approved relatively quickly (5 months) in 2011–2012, showing that rear patios can win approval. However, this was in RTO-M zoning, not NCT-MISSION, and the parking-lot conversion at 2214 Mission filed around the same time was ultimately withdrawn.

comparables.why_comparable: CUA for new bar use (Type 47) and outdoor activity area not at the front at 739–741 Valencia (144 m), NCT-VALENCIA district. Filed December 2010, approved April 2011 in ~4 months. This is a use decision combining bar and outdoor seating approvals.
comparables.key_takeaway: A bar plus non-front outdoor area in a nearby NCT district (Valencia) was approved in 4 months in 2010–2011, demonstrating that outdoor seating paired with a full bar can pass Commission review when the outdoor space is not at the street front and the concept fits neighborhood character.

comparables.why_comparable: CUA to legalize existing restaurant (Bissap Baob) at 3372 19th St (135 m), NCT-MISSION district. Filed September 2018, approved March 2019 in ~6 months with extensive conditions including hours (Tue–Sun 11 am to 1:45 am), noise, odor, sidewalk maintenance and community liaison. This is a use decision for a restaurant in the Mission Alcohol SUD.
comparables.key_takeaway: Restaurant CUAs in NCT-MISSION within the Mission Alcohol Special Use District are approved with conditions tailored to the high-density corridor: hours caps (here until 1:45 am), sidewalk monitoring within a one-block radius, soundproofing, odor control, and a mandatory community liaison officer before building permit issuance.

comparables.why_comparable: Agency referral (DPH) for restaurant at 2224 Mission (17 m away, next door), NCT-MISSION district. Filed September 2019, approved October 2019 in <1 month. This is an agency referral, not a use decision, so it confirms only that a continuation restaurant use was permitted; it does not reveal Commission hearing standards.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved a DPH restaurant referral next door at 2224 Mission in under a month, but this was an agency referral for an existing use, not a discretionary CUA. It shows the immediate block supports restaurant activity but says nothing about whether a new outdoor seating CUA would be approved.

comparables.why_comparable: Agency referral (DPH) for continuation restaurant use at 3382 18th St (80 m), NCT-MISSION district. Filed January 2021, approved January 2021 in ~1 week as a continuation under Planning Code §754 and §249.60. This is an agency referral.
comparables.key_takeaway: Continuation restaurant uses in NCT-MISSION are routinely approved by Planning staff as agency referrals within days under the continuation-of-use provisions. This pattern confirms that the district supports restaurant uses but does not predict discretionary CUA outcomes for new outdoor seating.

patterns.pattern: Outdoor seating CUAs at the rear of existing bar or restaurant uses in NCT districts near Mission Street were approved in 4–9 months in 2011–2017, while a prior application for parking-lot outdoor seating at 2214 Mission (noted in the FLAGS as withdrawn after 21 months) presents a cautionary precedent at this exact site.

Restaurant CUAs in the Mission Alcohol Special Use District (NCT-MISSION) approved 2018–2019 carried extensive standard conditions: hours limits, noise and odor controls, daily sidewalk monitoring within a one-block radius, garbage enclosure, and appointment of a community liaison before building permit issuance.

Agency referrals (DPH, ABC) for continuation restaurant uses in NCT-MISSION are routinely approved by Planning staff in days to weeks under Planning Code §754 continuation provisions; they do not require Commission hearings and offer no insight into discretionary CUA standards.

Outdoor activity areas approved in nearby NCT districts were described as being 'at the rear' or 'not located at the front,' suggesting that street-fronting or side parking-lot patios may face different scrutiny than rear yards.

Only 6 dated use decisions within 1,000 ft in the last 5 years: 2 approved, 2 approved with conditions, 2 withdrawn; this small sample prevents calculating a meaningful approval rate but shows that withdrawals do occur in this corridor.

findings.text: Zoning district NCT-MISSION: a Restaurant on the first story is a conditional use per Planning Code § 754.

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District requires Conditional Use for any proposed Restaurant in the sub-area east of the Mission Street NCT western boundary and north of Cesar Chavez; this parcel lies inside that sub-area (Planning Code § 249.60(f)(1)).

NCT-MISSION Table 754 Note 7 caps eating and drinking uses (Restaurants, Limited Restaurants and Bars) in the district at 167 total, and a new one is not permitted if it would take the total above that; the records do not show how many exist.

A prior CUA application (2010.0852C) for outdoor seating on adjacent property used as surface parking at 2214 Mission St was filed September 2010 and withdrawn June 2012 after 21 months, with no decision rendered.

Two comparable outdoor seating CUAs nearby were approved: 2011.0894C at 3481 18th St (rear outdoor area, RTO-M, approved January 2012, 5 months from filing) and 2017-003058CUA at 2323 Mission St (rear outdoor area for bar/restaurant, NCT-MISSION, approved December 2017, 9 months from filing).

Restaurant CUA 2018-012727CUA at 3372 19th St (135 m away, NCT-MISSION, Mission Alcohol SUD) was approved March 2019 with conditions including hours (Tue–Sun 11 am to 1:45 am), daily sidewalk monitoring within a one-block radius, soundproofing, odor control, and appointment of a community liaison before building permit issuance.

findings.text: The description states alcohol_transaction is 'licence_already_held' but does not give alcohol_type (beer and wine, or full liquor), so which ABC license type and whether Planning Code § 249.60(b)(1)(A) bona fide eating place transfer provisions apply cannot be established.

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District § 249.60(b)(1)(A) permits a Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place to serve alcohol and allows its license to be transferred from inside or outside the district, adding no Conditional Use for the license itself.

The Mission Alcohol SUD requires every liquor establishment to comply with § 202.2 operating conditions, and new, relocated or expanded ones must provide exterior lighting, keep window signage to 33% and maintain 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades (Planning Code § 249.60(d)).

The health permit application is referred to the Planning Department for zoning review per Planning Code § 175(a).

expected_conditions.condition: Hours of operation capped at closing by 1:45 am or earlier (typically 10 pm for outdoor areas under § 202.2(a)(7) unless a later hour is granted by CUA).
expected_conditions.basis: Restaurant CUA 2018-012727CUA at 3372 19th St in NCT-MISSION Mission Alcohol SUD was conditioned to operate Tue–Sun 11 am to 1:45 am. Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) allows outdoor activity areas as of right only if they close by 10 pm.

expected_conditions.condition: Daily sidewalk monitoring and cleaning within a one-block radius during business hours, in compliance with Police Code Article 1 § 34 and DPW Street and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition imposed on eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION per Motion No. 20397 (2018-012727CUA): 'the operator shall be responsible for daily monitoring of the sidewalk within a one-block radius of the subject business to maintain the sidewalk free of paper or other litter associated with the business during business hours.'

expected_conditions.condition: Soundproofing and noise control so that incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises and fixed-source equipment noise does not exceed San Francisco Noise Ordinance decibel levels.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition for eating and drinking uses in enclosed spaces per 2018-012727CUA Motion: 'the premises shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises.'

expected_conditions.condition: Odor control equipment installed and maintained to prevent noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises, in compliance with BAAQMD standards.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition for restaurants per 2018-012727CUA Motion: 'appropriate odor control equipment shall be installed in conformance with the approved plans and maintained to prevent any significant noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises.'

expected_conditions.condition: Appointment of a community liaison officer before building permit issuance, with name and contact information provided to the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition for CUAs in this corridor per 2018-012727CUA Motion: 'Prior to issuance of a building permit to construct the project and implement the approved use, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties.'

expected_conditions.condition: Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD operating requirements: exterior lighting, window signage limited to 33% of window area, and 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades (for new, relocated or expanded liquor establishments).
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 249.60(d) mandates these conditions for every new, relocated or expanded liquor establishment in the Mission Alcohol SUD and any with a license referred to Planning by ABC.

expected_conditions.condition: Garbage, recycling and composting storage in enclosed areas on the property, clearly labeled on building permit plans and meeting San Francisco Recycling Program standards.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition for eating and drinking uses per 2018-012727CUA Motion and Planning Department template conditions: 'Space for the collection and storage of garbage, composting, and recycling shall be provided within enclosed areas on the property and clearly labeled and illustrated on the building permit plans.'

expected_conditions.condition: Outdoor seating area limited to seated patrons only (no standing service), with alcohol service only inside the premises or by wait staff at the patron's outdoor seat, if § 202.2(a)(7) applies.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) allows outdoor activity areas for Restaurant or Limited Restaurant as of right only if 'seated areas only, no standing' and 'alcohol dispensed only inside the premises or by wait staff at the patron's outdoor seat.'

filing_playbook.action: Request a written Letter of Determination from San Francisco Planning confirming the current count of eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION against the 167 cap, whether the outdoor area as proposed meets § 202.2(a)(7) limits, and the CUA pathway.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a brief letter to the Zoning Administrator describing the restaurant use with outdoor seating in a parking lot at 2214 Mission St, parcel 3589/002, NCT-MISSION district, and ask three questions: (1) How many eating and drinking uses (Restaurants, Limited Restaurants and Bars) are currently in the district toward the 167 cap in Table 754 Note 7? (2) Does the parking-lot outdoor seating area as described meet all limits of Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) to be permitted as of right, or does it require Conditional Use Authorization? (3) Does the Restaurant use itself require CUA under § 249.60(f)(1) and § 754 given the district count? Allow 4–6 weeks for a written response before filing a CUA or building permit.

filing_playbook.action: If the Letter confirms a CUA is required, file a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning for the Restaurant use and outdoor activity area.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Prepare the CUA application package: project description emphasizing that this is an existing restaurant (if true) or a new restaurant within the Mission Alcohol SUD bona fide eating place provisions, outdoor seating in a private parking lot not on the public right-of-way, limited cooking, no late-night hours, and compliance with § 202.2 good-neighbor policies. Include a site plan showing the parking-lot patio layout, seating count, barriers or fencing, and distance from residential windows. Include a neighborhood outreach summary documenting pre-application meetings with the Mission neighborhood association and abutting residents. Address the 2010 withdrawn CUA in the narrative: explain what has changed (e.g., revised design, reduced footprint, noise mitigation measures) and why this application will succeed. Emphasize compatibility with the high-density Mission corridor and cite the t…

filing_playbook.action: In parallel with or after the CUA application, register the business entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation) and obtain an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization (LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (ARTS-GS, $100) online at the California Secretary of State bizfile portal; allow 1–10 days. Apply for an EIN online at irs.gov (free, issued immediately Mon–Fri). These are prerequisites for the San Francisco business registration, sellers permit, and all other licenses.

filing_playbook.action: Register for a San Francisco Business Account Number (BAN) with the Treasurer & Tax Collector and file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online for a Business Registration Certificate within 30 days of starting business; fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g., $55 up to $100k, $625 at $1–1.5M for 2026–27, plus $4 state fee); allow 1–5 days. File the Fictitious Business Name statement (if the public name differs from the entity name) in person or by mail with the SF County Clerk, then publish the statement in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks and file proof of publication within 45 days; total elapsed time ~35 days, fee ~$60–120. Every other city department asks for the BAN, so complete this step before filing health or building permit applications.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a California Seller's Permit from CDTFA and register as an employer with EDD if hiring employees.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online for a Seller's Permit at CDTFA (free, often issued same day); this is required before ABC will issue an alcohol license. If hiring employees, register with EDD for payroll taxes within 15 days of paying more than $100 in wages (free, online, 1–7 days). Obtain workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund before the first employee starts (no government fee, but coverage is mandatory from day one).

filing_playbook.action: If the concept includes tenant improvements for the parking-lot patio (surfaces, utilities, barriers) or any kitchen work, submit a building permit application with DBI and route it to Planning for zoning review and DPH for plan check.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Prepare construction drawings stamped by a licensed architect showing patio construction (deck, barriers, drainage, lighting, utilities), any kitchen or hood upgrades for limited cooking, and ADA access. Submit the building permit application online and select 'health' and 'planning' as routing stations. DBI will send the application to Planning for zoning review; if the CUA has been approved, Planning clears the permit over the counter. DPH plan check for a remodeled food facility costs $828–$2,207 flat fee and takes 21–60 days. Schedule a DPH pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection at least two weeks in advance. DBI building permit fees are a percentage of construction valuation; allow 14–120 days for permit issuance depending on plan complexity, and budget $800–$15,000 for small tenant improvement work.

filing_playbook.action: If the concept involves a grease interceptor or any cooking equipment, submit FOG program registration paperwork to SFPUC before the final building inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Contact SFPUC Wastewater Enterprise for a Discharger Category assignment (1–3) based on the limited cooking described; install the required grease-capturing equipment per the category, and submit the Installation Verification Form to SFPUC to earn a 14.2% sewer bill reduction. Allow 14–45 days for registration, with fees up to $500 for plan review if required. An undersized or missing interceptor will block DBI final sign-off.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for a Health Permit to Operate at least one month before the planned opening, after DPH plan check is approved and a certified food safety manager is on staff.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online through the DPH Environmental Health portal with the BAN, Location ID (LIN) and federal EIN. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (includes initial inspection; 2026–27 annual license fee is $0 for restaurants). Ensure one owner or employee has passed an ANSI-accredited food safety manager exam (ServSafe, Prometric, NRFSP; ~$125–$200 course plus exam, valid 5 years) and all food employees have California Food Handler Cards (~$7–$15, online, valid 3 years). Schedule the pre-opening inspection at least two weeks in advance; the permit is issued after the inspector confirms the facility matches approved plans, equipment is installed, hand sinks and hot water are operational, and the food safety manager certificate is on file. Walk the space against the DPH checklist a week before the inspection to avoid failed inspections that push openings by 2–3 weeks. Allow 14–4…

filing_playbook.action: If the concept involves recorded music, obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses before opening.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online for blanket licenses from ASCAP and BMI (not government permits, but required by federal copyright law for any business playing music publicly). Annual fees are formula-based on occupancy and music use (typically $300–$2,500 each); licenses are effective immediately upon payment. Most venues need both because their catalogs do not overlap. Alternatively, subscribe to a licensed commercial music service (e.g., Soundtrack Your Brand) that includes performance rights. This takes under a week and operators often forget it entirely, then receive demand letters after opening.

filing_playbook.action: If alcohol is served, confirm that the existing ABC license held by the operator is active, transferred to this address, and the correct type (Type 41 for beer and wine, Type 47 for full liquor in a restaurant).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Contact ABC to verify the license status and submit a premises-to-premises transfer application if the license is currently at another address. ABC will refer the transfer to San Francisco Planning for zoning sign-off; if the CUA has been approved, Planning will approve the referral. A Type 41 (beer and wine, eating place) transfer takes 60–120 days if unprotested; a Type 47 (full liquor, eating place) transfer takes 90–240 days including escrow if purchased on the open market ($100k–$450k in SF). Ensure all alcohol servers and managers complete Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) training within 60 days of hire (ABC RBS Portal, $3 registration plus ~$10–$25 course, 1–7 days). Post the ABC license and RBS certification list on site for inspections.

timeline_cost.notes: The day range is the time to obtain the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to approval per the 2017-003058CUA and 2018-012727CUA comparables) and Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days after plan check approval). This is a time to approval for those two approvals in the entitlement path. It does not include time to a withdrawal or a denial. The cost range covers the CUA filing fee (~$3,100 base for no-construction CUA, 2026–27 schedule), health plan check ($828–$2,207), health permit to operate ($470), business registration ($55–$625 depending on gross receipts), and entity formation ($70–$150), totaling roughly $4,900–$6,500 in government fees. If a building permit is required for patio construction or kitchen work, add 14–120 days and $800–$15,000 in DBI fees (shown as the high end of the range). The alcohol license row status is insufficient information so no ABC time or cost is included here; if a Type 41 or Type 47 transfer is needed, add 60–240 days and $1,000–$450,000 (license purchase cost) to both ranges. The zoning row status is further review, meaning a CUA is needed, and the outdoor row status is insufficient information, meaning the outdoor area may also need CUA or may be permitted as of right under § 202.2(a)(7); the playbook assumes both are resolved by the single Restaurant plus outdoor area CUA filed in Step 2, so the timeline reflects one CUA hearing. The 2010 withdrawn CUA at this exact address (21 months without decision per site history) is a red flag; the timeline here assumes a successful application with neighborhood support and revised design, not a repeat withdrawal.
